preconditions.description: The first line of input is a positive integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 26) representing the number of strings in the sequence.
The second line of input is a non-empty string q of lowercase Latin letters with length between 1 and 100, inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in stdin.split()[1])
preconditions.description: All characters in string q are lowercase Latin letters.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'NO' if not any(len(set(s[0] for s in sequence)) == k for sequence in possible_sequences(q, k)) else ('YES' in stdout and len(stdout.split()[1:]) == k and ''.join(stdout.split()[1:]) == q)
postconditions.description: If no beautiful sequence exists (i.e., no way to split q into k non-empty substrings with distinct first characters), output is exactly 'NO'. Otherwise, output starts with 'YES' followed by k lines representing a valid sequence s_1, ..., s_k where s_1 + ... + s_k = q and all first characters of s_i are distinct.

postconditions.expression: all(len(s) >= 1 for s in stdout.split()[1:]) if 'YES' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: Each string in the sequence is non-empty.

postconditions.expression: len(set(s[0] for s in stdout.split()[1:])) == k if 'YES' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: The first characters of all strings in the sequence are distinct.
